messages:
mia: Observed a pretty large regional gap in our prefix cache hit-rate after the recent kernel+batching rollout. us-west ~81% hit, eu-central ~46%, ap-south ~11%. p95 token latency up in eu by ~70ms. Can someone sanity-check profiler + logs? :frowning_face:

sam: Was this immediately after the kernel selection change (the one that landed last night)? Any correlation with the kernel fallback path or batching heuristics?

mia: yes, it started within the rollout window. I ran a quick flamegraph and a few replayed requests. Looks like KV key hashing + cache-lookup overhead increased for some sequence-length distributions. Also noticed the preprocessor normalization change — we now strip punctuation differently which seems to change key entropy.

tyler: can you paste the profiler snippet? Also did we change the cache key derivation ordering? I recall we removed route_zone from the key to reduce splay.

mia: snippet pasted below:
```text
flamegraph hotspots (eu):
- kv_lookup_async: 32%
- prefix_hashing: 14%
- kernel_dispatch: 9%
hot path shows more CPU on prefix_hashing due to regex normalize step.
```

leena: dropping route_zone *should* make keys more portable (good for cross-region reuse). Strange that eu dropped and us stayed high — maybe routing changed so eu gets a different set of prefixes now.

sam: infra-bot metrics: <https://grafana.redwood/replication/kv-lag?from=1783496000&to=1783504320> — shows replication lag spikes around 1783498000 during the deploy. devops-bot also posted a deploy: "kv-key-change v2" at 1783497900.

olga: I dug into key entropy distribution per-region. We removed truncation for long prompts in the new normalizer; small tail differences are producing unique keys at high cardinality. Combined with slightly different request mixes per region, that explodes unique key space in eu.

tyler: two quick hypotheses: (1) normalization changed cardinality -> lower reuse, (2) replication lag + routing threshold caused eu to miss while us served locals. Possible mitigations: stable truncation, canonicalize whitespace/punctuation, or reintroduce route_zone in key for locality.

mia: quick synthetic: re-enabled 256-char truncation + siphash64 for keys and ran a 30m replay against eu. Hit-rate improved 46% -> 64% within 30 minutes. p95 tokens down ~50ms. ap-south still low because replication backlog was ~90s there.

leena: For cold-region mitigation we should combine: (1) proactive prefetch for top-k prefixes for each model, (2) async replication splay with jittered TTLs, (3) routing fallback to region with stable cache when replication lag > threshold.

sam: prefetching adds cost — can we be smarter? Only prefetch prefixes with >X QPS or with high value (business metric). Also add a per-region cache-key cardinality metric so we can alarm before it tanks.

olga: agreed. I propose a lightweight scoreboard service that aggregates top prefixes by weight (QPS * token_count) and exposes prefetch_candidates API. We can keep prefetch limited to top-10k prefixes per model and tier.

tyler: on routing: propose policy param `prefer_local_with_threshold(0.6)` — if local hit_rate > 60% prefer local, otherwise route to global replica (us) or fallback to nearest zone that has the prefix. Also add logic to prefer cached model-variants.

mia: tried a small warmup experiment: enable prefetch-on-first-miss for top-5k prefixes + the truncation rollback. eu hit-rate jumped 46% -> 69% after 10 minutes, p95 down ~50ms. ap-south improved marginally because of replication backlog.

sam: we should gate this behind an opt-in flag and run 24h canary in eu/ap-south before full rollout. Also add cardinality and prefetch-cost dashboards.

olga: implementation note: prefetch should be async and backpressure-aware. If replication lag > 30s, prefer routing fallback rather than piling prefetch jobs into region.

devops-bot: Alert cleared — replication-lag spike resolved (1783504000). No further deploys since the incident.

mia: Action items: I'll open an RFC describing: key-derivation rollback + truncation + hashing, plus routing policy proposal. @tyler and @olga to prototype prefetch scoreboard and candidate API. @sam to add cardinality metric + dashboards. We'll run a 24h warmup experiment in eu and ap-south and reconvene. :thumbsup:
